# gaba_excites

> A browser simulator of current-clamp recording from a cortical
> regular-spiking pyramidal neuron, for teaching excitability. It runs
> entirely on the reader's machine: no server, no upload, no analytics.

This is a hand-maintained plain-text summary of https://gaba.tonydefazio.com/
for readers that do not run JavaScript. The full account, with every equation,
is at https://gaba.tonydefazio.com/methods (static HTML).

## What it does

- Two models, chosen from a menu:
  - the regular-spiking (RS) pyramidal cell of Pospischil et al. 2008
    (Biol Cybern 99:427, doi:10.1007/s00422-008-0263-8; ModelDB 123623): one
    compartment, Traub INa and IKd, slow M-type IK for adaptation;
  - the mouse GnRH neuron of Adams et al. 2018 (J Neurosci 38:1249,
    doi:10.1523/JNEUROSCI.2988-17.2017), negative-feedback parameter set:
    Markov INaF, INaP, IA, IK, T-type and HVA ICa, IS, Ih, IKCa, calcium pool.
- The user sets whole-cell passive properties — Rin (as measured at rest),
  Cm (sets cell size; channel densities stay fixed) and holding current — and
  electrode properties: series resistance, bridge balance, pipette capacitance.
- Runs families of current steps (first/increment/count, or any list) and
  reports rheobase (refinable to 1 pA), spike threshold (dV/dt >= 20 V/s),
  AP peak and half-width, measured Rin, and the F–I curve (mean and initial
  rate); F–I curves can be pinned for comparison and exported as CSV.
- Two kinds of noise: recording noise (filtered Gaussian plus mains hum, on
  the recorded trace only) and membrane noise (an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck current
  the cell feels).
- Adds conductance-based glutamate (E = 0 mV) and GABA-A PSCs (E_GABA
  variable, default -80 mV), each with rate, peak conductance, rise and decay,
  Poisson or regular timing, from a seeded generator.

## Validation

Pyramidal cell: spike counts match NEURON 9.0.2 running the original ModelDB
mechanisms exactly for steps of 500–1500 pA, and every spike time agrees
within 0.2 ms (dt = 0.01 ms).

GnRH neuron: transcribed from the paper (no public code exists to compare
against). It reproduces what the paper reports: -6 pA holds it at -70 mV, and
500 ms steps of 0/6/12/18/24/30 pA give 0/0/0/1/4/6 spikes, as in its Fig. 7F.

## The result it is named for

On the published pyramidal cell, with clock-like GABA (200 Hz, 3 nS, 0.5/10 ms),
rheobase is 561 pA without GABA, 765 pA with E_GABA = -80 mV, 628 pA at
-60 mV (GABA depolarizes the cell yet still inhibits, by shunting), 560 pA at
-50 mV (neutral), and 457 pA at -35 mV (excitatory). The crossover is about
11 mV below spike threshold.

## Limits

One compartment; no Ih, calcium currents, NMDA, GABA-B, plasticity or
chloride dynamics; current clamp only; the published cell's Rin (32 MOhm) is
a high-conductance, in-vivo-like value.

## Source

https://github.com/syncytium2/gaba_excites (MIT). A command line
(`node scripts/fi.ts`) runs the same code without a browser.
